from pysat.solvers import Glucose4
from pysat.card import CardEnc, EncType
from pysat.formula import IDPool

G = 30  # golfers
W = 8   # weeks
K = 10  # groups per week
S = 3   # group size

vpool = IDPool()
def x(w, p, g):
    return vpool.id(('x', w, p, g))
def m(w, p, q):  # p<q, same group in week w
    return vpool.id(('m', w, p, q))

clauses = []

# Each golfer in exactly one group each week
for w in range(W):
    for p in range(G):
        lits = [x(w,p,g) for g in range(K)]
        cnf = CardEnc.equals(lits=lits, bound=1, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.pairwise)
        clauses.extend(cnf.clauses)

# Each group has exactly S players
for w in range(W):
    for g in range(K):
        lits = [x(w,p,g) for p in range(G)]
        cnf = CardEnc.equals(lits=lits, bound=S, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.seqcounter)
        clauses.extend(cnf.clauses)

# Symmetry: week 0 fixed: players 3g, 3g+1, 3g+2 in group g
for g in range(K):
    for i in range(S):
        clauses.append([x(0, 3*g+i, g)])

# m(w,p,q) iff x(w,p,g) and x(w,q,g) for some g
# m(w,p,q) -> OR_g (x(w,p,g) AND x(w,q,g))  -- weak direction
# We need: if p,q in same group in week w, then at most one such week
# Define: same(w,p,q) = 1 if p,q in same group in week w
# Simpler: for each pair p<q, for each week w, define same_wpq variable
# same_wpq <=> exists g: x(w,p,g)=x(w,q,g)=1
# Use: same_wpq -> x(w,p,g) equiv x(w,q,g) for all g? not quite
# Alternative: for each pair p<q and week w, at most one g has both.
# And: sum over w of "same in week w" <= 1.

# Define y(w,p,q,g) = x(w,p,g) AND x(w,q,g). For p<q.
# m(w,p,q) = OR_g y(w,p,q,g)
# Then sum_w m(w,p,q) <= 1.

# Simpler encoding: for each pair p<q and each week w, define same via:
# same(w,p,q) <- x(w,p,g) AND x(w,q,g)  for each g
# For upper bound use: sum_w sum_g (x(w,p,g) AND x(w,q,g)) <= 1
# But AND isn't directly a literal. Introduce aux z(w,p,q,g).

# Actually easier: for each pair p<q, for each week w: at most one common group.
# And forbid pair meeting more than once. 
# Introduce meet(w,p,q): if both x(w,p,g) and x(w,q,g), then meet(w,p,q).
# Add: x(w,p,g) AND x(w,q,g) -> meet(w,p,q)
# Then sum_w meet(w,p,q) <= 1.

for p in range(G):
    for q in range(p+1, G):
        meets = []
        for w in range(W):
            mv = m(w,p,q)
            meets.append(mv)
            for g in range(K):
                # x(w,p,g) AND x(w,q,g) -> mv
                clauses.append([-x(w,p,g), -x(w,q,g), mv])
        cnf = CardEnc.atmost(lits=meets, bound=1, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.seqcounter)
        clauses.extend(cnf.clauses)

print("clauses:", len(clauses), "vars:", vpool.top)

solver = Glucose4()
for c in clauses:
    solver.add_clause(c)

res = solver.solve()
print("result:", res)
if res:
    model = set(solver.get_model())
    schedule = [0]*(W*G)
    for w in range(W):
        for p in range(G):
            for g in range(K):
                if x(w,p,g) in model:
                    schedule[w*G+p] = g
                    break
    print(schedule)
    # verify
    from itertools import combinations
    pair_weeks = {}
    ok = True
    for w in range(W):
        groups = {}
        for p in range(G):
            groups.setdefault(schedule[w*G+p], []).append(p)
        for g, ps in groups.items():
            if len(ps) != 3:
                ok=False; print("bad group size", w, g, ps)
            for a,b in combinations(ps,2):
                pair_weeks.setdefault((a,b), []).append(w)
    for pair, ws in pair_weeks.items():
        if len(ws) > 1:
            ok = False; print("pair", pair, "meets", ws)
    print("verified:", ok)
